item.title: Binance says customers pulled $4.7 billion after its $6.3 billion hack
item.description: The exchange reopened withdrawals after a 48-hour freeze following the theft, which the FBI has linked to the North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.
item.content:encoded: Binance said Monday that customers had withdrawn a net $4.72 billion from the exchange since it reopened withdrawals on Sunday morning. The company had frozen withdrawals for roughly 48 hours after disclosing a $6.3 billion theft, which it has called potentially the largest financial heist in history. The exchange reported $2.7 billion of inflows after reopening, and said withdrawal volumes had since declined and stabilized. The Federal Bureau of Investigation has attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a hacking group the agency links to North Korea. Binance co-chief executive Yi He said the exchange's "top priority right now is to ensure the environment is secure, after which users can withdraw their funds." Binance said it is covering customer losses with company funds, having already raised $6 billion from its corporate treasury, an insurance fund and reserves set aside for security breaches. The stablecoin issuer Circle said it had frozen more than $1.1 billion in USDC tied to the theft. Bitcoin, which had fallen to a six-week low after the hack became public, had recovered to around $78,000 by Monday. Spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded $643 million of outflows the Friday before Binance reopened withdrawals, and more than $1.3 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated in the aftermath of the hack, according to the reporting. North Korea-linked hackers have stolen a combined $7.4 billion from crypto platforms in 2026. Neptune Digital Assets Corp (TSXV: NDA) fell 5.88% to CAD0.48, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "digital asset." Dmg Blockchain Solutions Inc (TSXV: DMGI) fell 4.88% to CAD0.39, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "blockchain." Both moves fall on the same day as Binance's disclosure; nothing in the available data ties one to the other.

item.title: Myriad Uranium closes its $1 million purchase of an Argentine project
item.description: The CSE-listed explorer paid cash and shares for 100% of the Los Altares uranium project in the Cerro Solo district.
item.content:encoded: Myriad Uranium Corp. (CSE: M; OTCQB: MYRUF; FSE: C3Q) said Monday it has closed its previously announced acquisition of the Los Altares uranium project in central Chubut Province, Argentina, from Green Shift Commodities Ltd. (TSXV: GCOM). The deal was first announced October 13, 2026, and the underlying share purchase agreement is dated October 9, 2026. Myriad paid $300,000 in cash plus 1,571,268 of its common shares, valued at $0.4455 per share, or about $700,000, bringing total consideration to $1,000,000 for a 100% interest in Buenavida Metales S.A., the Argentine company that holds the project's mineral claims. Green Shift retains a 2% net smelter return royalty on the project, with Myriad holding an option to repurchase half of that royalty, 1%, for $1,000,000. The shares issued to Green Shift as part of the consideration are subject to a four-month hold period, expiring March 1, 2027. Los Altares covers 55,000 hectares in the Cerro Solo uranium district and is adjacent to the Cerro Solo deposit and the historical Los Adobes mine, according to the release, which also described the project as carrying significant historical drilling data and approved environmental impact assessments. Separately, Myriad said it issued 150,000 stock options to a consultant, exercisable at $0.39 per share, vesting immediately and expiring October 30, 2031. Myriad chief executive Thomas Lamb said the deal "continues Myriad's strategy of acquiring projects with significant historic work in known uranium districts and with low up-front and ongoing costs and strong leverage to the uranium price."

item.title: China's robot makers are racing to build AI 'brains', not just bodies
item.description: Chinese embodied-AI startups raised about $13 billion in the first half of 2026, five times the prior year, as the industry shifts focus from humanoid stunts to software.
item.content:encoded: Chinese robotics companies that spent years building humanoids capable of running, dancing and performing backflips are now shifting resources into the software that could make those machines useful across a wider range of jobs, Reuters reported from Beijing. Chinese embodied-AI companies raised 93.5 billion yuan, or about $13 billion, across 322 deals in the first half of 2026 — five times the amount raised a year earlier, according to the research firm ITjuzi. Spirit AI co-founder Gao Yang said "the brain is indeed the weakest link in the complete robotics stack." Hangzhou-based Unitree, one of the world's largest humanoid robot makers by shipments, has about 30 researchers working on AI that predicts how objects behave. Ant Group's robotics unit, Robbyant, has trained a model on 160,000 hours of material, including 50,000 hours of human-guided robot movements, across 20 robot configurations from 17 different brands. DexForce, which trains robots in computer-generated environments, says it can prepare some industrial tasks for deployment within six to eight hours, with success rates above 99.9% in specified precision operations, according to chief operating officer Nicole Yang. The Chinese battery maker CATL said Spirit AI's robots achieved an insertion success rate above 99% connecting flexible wires during its battery-pack testing. American startups including Physical Intelligence, Skild AI and Generalist are pursuing a similar goal: software that lets a robot learn a new task without lengthy retraining. Three Chinese companies — X Square, Galaxea and Spirit AI — have each reached valuations of about $3 billion, and Hong Kong-listed UBTech advertised a chief scientist role paying up to 124 million yuan, or about $18 million, including equity and benefits. Shanghai-based ZenGen Labs founder Dermot McGrath concluded that the profit margin in robotics will come from the software rather than the hardware, according to the reporting. Unitree founder Wang Xingxing said a future version of the underlying AI models could bring robotics its own "ChatGPT moment" if robots can complete most tasks in unfamiliar environments from spoken instructions alone. item.title: Live Energy Minerals issues 120,000 shares to option a New Brunswick property
item.description: The CSE-listed junior's first tranche under an October 15 option agreement covers two uranium-copper claims near Plaster Rock, with no cash payments required.
item.content:encoded: Live Energy Minerals Corp. (CSE:LIVE; OTC:GTREF) said it completed the issuance of 120,000 common shares on October 30, 2026, at a deemed price of $0.20 per share, representing a deemed value of $24,000. The shares were issued as the initial tranche payment under an option agreement, dated October 15, 2026, granting Live Energy the right to acquire a 100% interest in the Plaster Rock property in New Brunswick. The Plaster Rock property comprises two mineral claims totalling 73 units, which the release describes as a uranium-copper property. Under the option agreement, Live Energy must issue a further 1,000,000 common shares on or before October 30, 2027, and a further 2,880,000 common shares on or before October 30, 2028. Each of the later tranches will be priced at the closing price of Live Energy's shares on the last trading day before issuance, under the policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange, the company said. The option carries no cash payments and no minimum exploration-expenditure commitments. The optionor retains a 2% net smelter returns royalty on the property. Live Energy may purchase one-half of that royalty, equal to 1 percentage point, at any time for $500,000, the release said. The 120,000 shares issued under the first tranche are subject to a statutory hold period expiring March 1, 2027, pursuant to applicable Canadian securities laws, the company said. The release does not designate its dollar figures as Canadian or US currency. Live Energy Minerals also holds the Mesa Top Mine and Section 20 uranium claims in New Mexico and has optioned its McDermitt Lithium East project in Nevada to US Critical Metals Corp., according to the release.

item.title: Russian strikes knock out power for hundreds of thousands in Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian drones struck a Russian missile plant in Rostov and caused significant damage in Nizhny Novgorod the same night, as a local ceasefire held elsewhere.
item.content:encoded: Russian missile and drone strikes hit power infrastructure across four Ukrainian regions overnight into Sunday, leaving hundreds of thousands of households without electricity, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Ukraine's air force said it shot down 371 of 433 long-range Russian drones launched since Saturday evening, according to Reuters, which did not specify how many struck their targets. Ukraine struck back at targets inside Russia. Drones hit the Kamensky plant in Russia's Rostov region, which Ukraine says is involved in missile manufacturing, Reuters reported. Nizhny Novgorod governor Gleb Nikitin said a separate, large-scale drone attack caused significant damage to an industrial facility in his region, which is home to the NORSI oil refinery, one of Russia's largest. Russia's Defence Ministry said it downed 235 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight. A six-day local ceasefire around the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky held through its final day, Reuters reported, even as fighting continued elsewhere along the front line and both sides kept up long-range strikes. Ukraine says it supports a broader ceasefire specifically covering energy-infrastructure targets, and says Russia has not agreed to one. US President Donald Trump has asked Ukraine to stop striking Russian oil refineries, Reuters reported, saying such strikes have helped push up diesel prices ahead of US midterm elections. Five of the eight traded; none rose and three fell, for a median move of -2.07%, against a -2.77% decline for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp. (CSE:QESS) fell 11.11% to C$0.24, qualifying for the theme because its registered name contains "defence." Alchemy Labs Inc (TSXV:ALCH) fell 9.88% to C$0.73, in the theme because its sector label is "Aerospace & Defense." Kraken Robotics Inc (TSXV:PNG) fell 2.07% to C$3.78, its registered name being Kraken Robotics Inc. The declines fall on the same day as the strikes reported above. Neither the reporting on the strikes nor the quotes behind these moves draws any connection between the two, and none is implied here.

item.title: Eureka Metals wants $499,134 from shareholders at a penny a share
item.description: The rights offering precedes a proposed share consolidation of up to six-for-one, with rights expiring December 1.
item.content:encoded: Eureka Metals Corp. (CSE: ERKA) (OTCQB: UREKF) (FSE: S580), a Canadian mineral explorer holding titanium, vanadium, scandium and other polymetallic projects in Quebec and British Columbia, has launched a rights offering to raise up to $499,134. Holders of common shares as of November 6, 2026 will receive one transferable right for each share held. Each right entitles its holder to subscribe for one pre-consolidation common share at $0.01. Rights expire December 1, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. Toronto time, and the company expects the offering to close on or about December 2, 2026. Odyssey Trust Company is acting as rights agent. Eureka separately proposes to consolidate its shares on a basis of up to six pre-consolidation shares for every one post-consolidation share, with the final ratio to be set by the board. The company had 49,913,367 shares outstanding before the offering; if every right is exercised, that would roughly double to about 99,826,734 shares before the consolidation is applied. At the maximum six-for-one ratio and full exercise of the rights, Eureka would have approximately 16,637,789 shares outstanding following both the offering and the consolidation. The company says the consolidation remains subject to Canadian Securities Exchange approval, and shares are expected to continue trading under the ticker ERKA. The company said net proceeds from the rights offering, combined with its existing working capital, are expected to fund exploration and property costs, general and administrative expenses, and unallocated working capital. The offering is open to shareholders in all Canadian provinces and territories and in select international jurisdictions, excluding the United States. The release does not state whether the dollar figures in the offering are Canadian or U.S. currency. Eureka is a Canadian company listed primarily on the Canadian Securities Exchange, with secondary listings on the OTCQB in the United States and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange.

item.title: First Atlantic buys a Newfoundland property never tested for hydrogen
item.description: The explorer is paying 1,000,000 shares for 209 claims in the Bay of Islands Ophiolite Complex, where nearby ground shows historic chromite finds.
item.content:encoded: First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN) (OTCQB: FANCF) (FSE: P210) has signed an agreement, dated October 30, 2026, to acquire 100% of the North Arm Ophiolite Property on Newfoundland's west coast from two arm's-length vendors. The company will pay with 1,000,000 common shares issued at a deemed price of $0.55 each and will reimburse $51,250 in refundable security deposits the vendors had posted with the government of Newfoundland and Labrador. The property comprises three mineral licences totalling 209 claim cells across 52.25 square kilometres on the north shore of North Arm, within the Bay of Islands Ophiolite Complex. It lies about 25 kilometres north of First Atlantic's existing Ophiolite-X project. The company says the ground has seen limited modern exploration and has never been systematically tested for geologic hydrogen or for awaruite, a naturally occurring nickel-iron-cobalt alloy. First Atlantic points to historic chromite occurrences at nearby Blow Me Down and Springers Hill, and to active hydrogen-bearing alkaline springs at the nearby Tablelands, which the company says demonstrate ongoing serpentinization. The property itself carries no underlying royalty or option payments to a third party. Closing is conditional on TSX Venture Exchange acceptance and is expected about five business days afterward, by January 31, 2027. The 1,000,000 payment shares will be subject to a four-month-and-one-day hold period from issuance, the standard resale restriction attached to shares issued outside a prospectus offering. The company also granted 950,000 incentive stock options to directors and to an investor-relations consultant, exercisable at $0.55 per share for five years. The consultant's options vest quarterly over twelve months; the release does not state vesting terms for the options granted to directors. First Atlantic's existing project in the region, Pipestone XL, spans a 30-kilometre stretch of ophiolite complex and includes awaruite deposits the company says carry about 77% nickel content along with secondary chromium mineralization, according to the company's own description of its business.

item.title: Binance resumes bitcoin withdrawals after replacing $6 billion in stolen crypto
item.description: The exchange covered roughly 95% of October's $6.3 billion hack, which the FBI has tied to a North Korean hacking unit.
item.content:encoded: Binance began resuming withdrawals in phases on Sunday, starting with bitcoin shortly after 0600 GMT and followed within hours by ether, BNB, XRP, dogecoin and other tokens, after the exchange said it had covered roughly 95%, or about $6 billion, of the $6.3 billion in crypto stolen in October. The remaining 5%, in less liquid assets, is still being sourced, Binance said. The FBI said it had tied the theft to a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit it calls TraderTraitor, which the bureau said laundered the stolen assets by converting them into Ethereum. Asked about the attribution, President Trump said: "We don't know if it's North Korea — but if it is, we'll talk to North Korea about it." Binance funded the replacement tokens using half of its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users, along with portions of its futures insurance fund and corporate treasury, the exchange said. Co-chief executive Yi He said the company was committed to replenishing the Secure Asset Fund back to about $1 billion. Founder Changpeng Zhao thanked law enforcement for its help, saying "a tweet can't fully express our gratitude." Binance, described in the report as the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said the phased restart ultimately covered 15 crypto assets, beginning with bitcoin and followed by ether, BNB, XRP, dogecoin and the USDT and USDC stablecoins, restoring withdrawal access across the tokens affected by the October halt. The theme of digital-asset names on Canada's venture boards comprises 14 listed companies; five traded today, one higher and four lower, for a median move of -4.88% against -2.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of -2.11 percentage points on the day Binance announced the restored withdrawals. Neptune Digital Assets Corp (TSXV: NDA) fell 5.88% to $0.48, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "digital asset." Dmg Blockchain Solutions Inc (TSXV: DMGI) fell 4.88% to $0.39, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "blockchain." The moves and the Binance news fall on the same day; nothing here connects the two.

item.title: New Break seeks $550,000 to fund drilling at its Timmins-area gold project
item.description: The flow-through financing would fund exploration spending at the company's Moray project, 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, if it closes as planned.
item.content:encoded: New Break Resources Ltd. (CSE: NBRK) said October 30 that it intends to complete a non-brokered private placement of up to 2,500,000 flow-through common shares at $0.22 per share, for gross proceeds of up to $550,000. The company expects the offering to close within the next two business days, subject to acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange and other customary conditions. The shares qualify as flow-through shares within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada). New Break said the proceeds will be used for Canadian Exploration Expenses, which it will renounce to the purchasers of the shares with an effective date of no later than December 31, 2026, as stated in the release. The company said the proceeds raised through the offering will go toward ongoing drilling at its Moray gold project, located 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, in the Abitibi greenstone belt. The release gave no drill results or further technical detail on the current program. Qualified finders who introduce subscribers to the offering may receive a cash fee equal to 6% of the proceeds from those subscribers, plus finder's warrants equal to 6% of the flow-through shares sold to them, exercisable at $0.22 per share for 24 months from closing, according to the release. All securities issued under the offering, including any finder's warrants, are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, the standard resale restriction under Canadian securities law for this type of exemption. New Break describes itself as a Canadian mineral exploration company focused primarily on the Moray project, and also holds a 20% carried interest in the Sundog gold project in Nunavut. The release did not disclose the size of New Break's partner's interest in Sundog or any other terms of that arrangement.

item.title: A Southeast Asian conglomerate still awaits one approval for Altura's $3-million raise
item.description: Altura Energy extended the deadline to close its $3-million helium financing to November 30 while its investor's bank sign-off is pending.
item.content:encoded: Altura Energy Corp. (TSXV: ALTU) said October 30 that it has extended, to November 30, 2026, the deadline to complete a non-brokered private placement of 18,541,400 units at $0.1618 each, for gross proceeds of C$3 million. The TSX Venture Exchange has granted conditional acceptance of the offering, which the company first disclosed in a July 28, 2026 news release. Each unit under the offering comprises one common share and one share purchase warrant, exercisable at $0.25 for 36 months from the closing date. A non-brokered placement is one an issuer sells directly to subscribers rather than through an investment dealer, which is consistent with the release naming no agent or underwriter on the transaction. The sole subscriber is described in the release only as a leading Southeast Asian conglomerate; Altura's release does not name the investor. That investor has obtained approval from its own local Ministry of Finance to proceed, but the release said it is still awaiting a further approval from its state bank before the financing can close. Altura said the investor will have the right to nominate one member to the board of directors once the placement completes; the release did not disclose who might be nominated or any further governance terms attached to the investment beyond that right. The extension is the only change disclosed in the October 30 release; the unit count, the per-unit price and the warrant terms are unchanged from the July 28 announcement, according to the company. No new closing date beyond November 30, 2026, was given, and the release did not say what happens if that date passes without the state bank's approval. Altura describes itself as a helium-focused exploration company advancing prospects in the Holbrook Basin of Arizona, targeting helium for uses the company lists as healthcare, semiconductors, aerospace and other advanced-technology applications. The company also trades on the OTCQB under the symbol ALTUF and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under Y020.

item.title: Edgewater Wireless settles debenture interest in shares, including some to its own directors
item.description: The TSX Venture company will issue 1,421,982 shares at $0.05 to cover $71,100 in interest owed on debentures issued in 2022.
item.content:encoded: Edgewater Wireless Systems Inc. (TSXV: YFI) said October 30 that it will settle an aggregate of $71,100.01 owed in interest on its unsecured debentures, issued September 1, 2022, by issuing 1,421,982 common shares at a deemed price of $0.05 per share. The interest covers four quarterly obligations dated December 1, 2025, March 1, 2026, June 1, 2026 and September 1, 2026. Of the shares being issued, 265,995 are going to company directors, the release said. Edgewater said that participation triggers the related-party transaction requirements of Multilateral Instrument 61-101, which governs transactions between an issuer and its insiders. Edgewater said it qualifies for an exemption from the formal-valuation and minority-shareholder-approval requirements that would otherwise apply, because neither the fair value of the shares nor the debt being settled exceeds 25% of the company's market capitalization, as calculated under the instrument. The debt settlement remains subject to the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange, the company said. The release did not state when that approval is expected or what happens to the arrangement if it is not granted. Separately, Edgewater said it granted 900,000 stock options to employees and consultants at an exercise price of $0.05 per share. The options expire five years from the date of grant, according to the release. Edgewater also trades over the counter in the United States under the symbol KPIFF. The release gave no further detail on the company's current financial position or on why the interest was settled in shares rather than cash.

item.title: OpenAI cuts its funding target by $10 billion as AI stocks slide
item.description: The ChatGPT maker now seeks $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from a $30 billion target.
item.content:encoded: OpenAI has cut the target for its latest funding round by $10 billion, now seeking about $20 billion rather than the $30 billion it had been pursuing, according to a Financial Times report carried by Reuters. The company is also seeking a lower valuation, $1.25 trillion rather than the $1.4 trillion target. OpenAI had set a Friday deadline for investor commitments, Reuters reported. The reduction follows a selloff across technology stocks tied to concerns over the scale of AI infrastructure spending. Reuters reported the Nasdaq fell 2.9% on the day the cut was reported and is down 7.8% from its October 6 peak. Some investors have reduced the size of their commitments to the round, and the fund's 'first close' — the initial tranche of capital committed — is expected to come in below the revised $20 billion target. Reuters named several participants in the round, including the UAE-backed technology fund MGX, expected to be the largest investor, alongside Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz. OpenAI is pursuing a public listing in 2027, and Reuters reported the company had been keen to close this round ahead of rival Anthropic's anticipated listing, since the two companies draw on an overlapping investor base. item.title: Ashley Gold closes C$2.08-million private placement in two tranches
item.description: The final tranche raised C$631,275 at 6.5 and 8 cents a unit, pending Canadian Securities Exchange acceptance of the full offering.
item.content:encoded: Ashley Gold Corp., a Canadian mineral exploration company focused on gold and polymetallic deposits, has closed the second and final tranche of a non-brokered private placement. The tranche raised additional gross proceeds of C$631,275, taking the offering's aggregate gross proceeds, combined with a first tranche that closed October 19, 2026, to C$2,077,461.49. The release states the offering remains subject to final acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. The final tranche was split between two unit types. The company issued 6,635,000 non-flow-through units at C$0.065 per unit, for gross proceeds of C$431,275, and 2,500,000 flow-through units at C$0.08 per unit, for gross proceeds of C$200,000. Flow-through units carry tax deductions the company renounces to the subscriber; non-flow-through units do not. Each non-flow-through unit consists of one common share and one-half of a warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable at C$0.12 for 24 months. Each flow-through unit consists of one flow-through common share and one-half of a warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable at C$0.15 for 24 months. The company paid aggregate cash finder's fees of C$45,042 and issued 652,800 non-transferable finder warrants, exercisable between C$0.065 and C$0.08, in connection with the offering. All securities issued in the final tranche are subject to a statutory hold period expiring March 1, 2027. Net proceeds from the flow-through portion are earmarked for eligible Canadian exploration expenses that qualify as flow-through mining expenditures, which the company will renounce to subscribers effective December 31, 2026. Chief executive Darcy Christian called the financing the largest in the company's history, citing continued support from new and returning investors. Following the close, the company had 129,888,470 common shares outstanding. The release describes the company's flagship assets as 100%-owned claims in the Dryden area of Ontario, plus an optioned Icefield claim package in British Columbia.

item.title: Goliath Resources raises C$9.8 million without issuing a single warrant
item.description: The non-brokered flow-through placement, still subject to final TSX Venture Exchange approval, funds exploration at the Golddigger-Surebet gold project in BC's Golden Triangle.
item.content:encoded: Goliath Resources Limited, an explorer of precious-metals projects in the Golden Triangle of northwestern British Columbia, has closed a non-brokered private placement for gross proceeds of C$9,800,000. The company issued 6,057,000 flow-through common shares at a price of C$1.62 per share. No warrants were attached to the units, and the company paid no finder's fees or commissions in connection with the offering. The shares were issued as flow-through shares, which qualify under subsection 66(15) of Canada's Income Tax Act. That designation lets the company renounce the associated tax deductions for qualifying exploration expenditures to the subscribers who bought the shares, rather than claiming those deductions itself — a structure used to attract investors to exploration-stage mining financings. Goliath said the funds will go toward Canadian exploration expenses and flow-through mining expenditures on its Golddigger-Surebet Gold Project. The qualifying expenditures must be incurred by December 31, 2027, and the associated tax deductions renounced to subscribers by December 31, 2026. The offering remains subject to final acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange, the release states. The shares issued are subject to a statutory four-month hold period expiring March 1, 2027, under applicable Canadian securities law. Chief executive Roger Rosmus said the financing is "an insurance policy that further enhances our strong balance sheet and puts us in a stronger position, with ~C$27.5M in cash going into 2027 and our planned exploration drill program." The company describes its projects as sitting in "high quality geological settings and geopolitical safe jurisdictions amenable to mining in Canada." In 2026 it completed a fully funded 48,443-metre drill program on the Golddigger-Surebet project, for which assays are pending on 55 holes, following a 64,364-metre program in 2025.

item.title: US offers Audi tariff relief to keep its $4-billion Georgia plant
item.description: Audi wants its 15% tariff on EU imports cut to 7.5%; the Commerce Department is expected to settle near 10% to secure roughly 4,500 jobs.
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration has promised tariff relief to Audi to help secure the automaker's $4 billion assembly plant in Georgia, two sources briefed on the discussions told Reuters. The sources said US officials told Audi executives the government plans to offer a broader tariff relief program for automakers making significant investments in US production. Audi has pushed Washington to cut the 15% tariff it currently pays on vehicles imported from the European Union to 7.5%. The sources said the Commerce Department was expected to agree to a rate of around 10% instead. The plant is expected to assemble 200,000 SUVs a year and create approximately 4,500 jobs, according to the reporting. Construction is due to begin next year, with production starting in the early 2030s. Audi has said tariffs on autos, steel, aluminum and parts cost it roughly €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) last year. The company currently imports every vehicle it sells in the US market from factories in Europe or Mexico, which is what exposes it fully to the tariff rate rather than partially. Audi chief executive Gernot Doellner said the Georgia investment decision followed "many months of careful planning and intense negotiations," adding, "If the American president invites you, you accept the invitation." The Commerce Department did not immediately comment, and Audi declined comment on the tariff discussions. The reporting cites two anonymous sources for the substance of the talks, plus Doellner's own public statement and earlier reporting from the Wall Street Journal. Neither Audi nor the Commerce Department has confirmed the specific 10% figure the sources attribute to the department. None of the venture-listed names the bulletin tracks under its tariffs and trade theme traded today. With no trading to measure, there is no group move to report, and the bulletin names none of them — a thin day for the theme, not a judgment on it.

item.title: SK Hynix and Samsung tumble as Intel's weak outlook spooks chip investors
item.description: Disappointing US earnings from Intel, Amazon and Alphabet triggered a broad selloff in Asian chipmakers and tech suppliers on Friday.
item.content:encoded: Technology and chip-supplier stocks fell heavily across Asian markets on Friday, with South Korea's chip heavyweights among the hardest hit. Samsung Electronics fell 5.9% and SK Hynix 8.3%. In Japan, Murata Manufacturing dropped 11%, Advantest fell 5.8%, Tokyo Electron fell more than 5%, and SoftBank Group fell nearly 7%. Taiwan's TSMC slipped 1.8% and Foxconn 3%, according to Investing.com. The selloff followed an over 20% plunge in Intel's share price after the company gave weak fourth-quarter guidance. Amazon added to the pressure after missing both revenue and profit estimates for its most recent quarter, with the company's cash flow deteriorating further. Investing.com reported that the moves reflect mounting doubts that the money being poured into AI infrastructure will be profitable in the long term, prompting a rotation out of high-valuation technology names and into more defensive sectors of the market. item.title: First Lithium Minerals raises $1.44 million across a LIFE offering and placement
item.description: The financing combined a Listed Issuer Financing Exemption offering with a private placement, pricing units from 11 to 15 cents to fund exploration in Chile and Ontario.
item.content:encoded: First Lithium Minerals Corp. (CSE: FLM, OTC Pink: FLMCF, FSE: X28) explores for lithium and other alkali metals at the Salar de Ascotan in northern Chile, and for gold and critical metals at the Lidstone project in northwestern Ontario. The company said on October 29 that it has closed the second tranche of its Listed Issuer Financing Exemption, or LIFE, offering together with a concurrent private placement, for combined gross proceeds of $1,442,144. The LIFE tranche raised $597,345 through 2,466,773 non-flow-through units at $0.11 per unit and 2,173,333 flow-through units at $0.15 per unit. Every unit across both offerings — LIFE and private placement alike — carries one-half of a common share purchase warrant, with a whole warrant exercisable at $0.18 per share for three years from closing. The private placement units are subject to the standard statutory hold period of four months and one day from closing. The LIFE Offering units, consistent with the exemption's design, carry no such hold and are freely tradeable once issued. First Lithium paid cash finder's fees of $23,908 plus 220,542 finder's warrants at $0.11 in connection with the LIFE tranche, and $33,387 in cash plus 337,702 finder's warrants in connection with the private placement. item.title: DoorDash offers $65 a share, valuing Instacart at about $17 billion
item.description: The cash-and-stock bid is a 26% premium to Instacart's October 22 closing price, with the deal targeted to close by the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028.
item.content:encoded: DoorDash has agreed to acquire Instacart, which operates under the legal name Maplebear Inc., in a deal that values the grocery-delivery company at approximately $17 billion. Instacart shareholders will be able to elect one of three forms of consideration for each share held: $65.00 in cash, 0.3372 of a DoorDash share, or a combination of $48.75 in cash and 0.0843 of a DoorDash share. The stock portion of the total consideration is capped at 25% of the deal's aggregate value, with proration mechanics built in should stock elections be oversubscribed. The per-share price represents a 26% premium to Instacart's closing stock price on October 22, 2026, according to the companies' release. Instacart's board of directors unanimously approved the transaction, and shareholders holding approximately 19% of the company's outstanding shares have already agreed to vote in favour of the deal. DoorDash said it intends to fund the cash portion of the deal using cash on hand together with proceeds from new debt, and has arranged a 364-day bridge loan facility from JPMorgan Chase. The company said the transaction carries no financing condition and that it is targeting investment-grade credit ratings. DoorDash said the combination is expected to generate more than $500 million in annual synergies within several years of closing. Completion is expected by the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028. The deal still requires Instacart shareholder approval, clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust act in the United States, and regulatory approvals in Canada and Israel, along with other customary closing conditions. item.title: Aeon Strategies' crypto audit delay pushes its filing to December 31
item.description: The CSE-listed company has applied for a management cease-trade order to avoid a broader halt while its auditor works through complex crypto-related holdings.
item.content:encoded: Aeon Strategies Ltd. (CSE: AEON, OTCQB: CLDVF, FSE: WQ40), formerly known as Cloud3 Ventures Inc., has updated its timeline for filing annual financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2026. The company now expects to file its audited annual filings, management's discussion and analysis and the related CEO and CFO certifications on or before December 31, 2026 — nearly a month later than the December 4, 2026 date it had previously disclosed. The company's auditor, Davidson & Company LLP, told Aeon that the delay is due to two factors: limited availability on the auditor's side, and the additional time required to complete audit procedures relating to the company's crypto-related investments, which the release says are more complex to audit than in prior years. To manage the consequences of the late filing, Aeon has applied to its principal regulator for a management cease trade order. If granted, an MCTO would prohibit only the company's chief executive officer and chief financial officer from trading in Aeon's securities until the annual filings are submitted — leaving ordinary shareholders free to continue trading. The release states that if the management cease trade order is not granted, securities regulators may instead issue a general cease trade order prohibiting all trading in Aeon's securities, a broader measure that would affect every shareholder rather than only its two senior officers. Until the annual filings are complete, Aeon is required to issue a default status report every two weeks by news release, under the continuous disclosure provisions of National Policy 12-203 covering defaulting reporting issuers. For investors, the distinction matters: an MCTO limits only who can trade, not whether the stock keeps trading at all, while a general cease trade order would stop every shareholder from buying or selling until the annual filings catch up. Aeon's application for the narrower order is still pending regulatory approval.

item.title: Steadright's insiders are expected to buy most of the second tranche

item.title: SK Hynix is handing shareholders $75 billion after a sevenfold profit jump
item.description: The chipmaker's operating profit rose more than sevenfold to 83.3 trillion won as AI-driven demand for memory chips sold out capacity into 2029.
item.content:encoded: SK Hynix said on Tuesday it will return approximately 100 trillion won, or about $75 billion, to shareholders this year, after third-quarter operating profit surged more than sevenfold to 83.3 trillion won from 11.4 trillion won a year earlier. Quarterly revenue rose 328% to 104.6 trillion won. The company is the world's largest maker of high-bandwidth memory chips used in artificial-intelligence data centres. The shareholder return is split between roughly 30 trillion won in cash dividends and 60 trillion won in share repurchases and cancellations, the latter figure including the 40 trillion won in buybacks the company had already announced in August. Shares in SK Hynix rose as much as 9.4% following the announcement. Chief financial officer Kim Woo-hyun said the company expects AI investment momentum to continue, with customers' AI spending translating into broader adoption of AI services and tangible business results. Analyst Ryu Young-ho of NH Investment & Securities said the results had eased many of the market's concerns, with earnings coming in ahead of expectations. SK Hynix said it has sold out its high-bandwidth memory and DRAM chip production through 2029 and has signed long-term supply agreements with 14 major customers covering more than half of its planned 2027-2028 production capacity. The company said it expects memory-chip demand to continue exceeding supply through 2030. item.title: Rush Gold adds two Nevada gold properties and a 40-year mining veteran as chairman

item.content:encoded: Rush Gold Corp. (CSE: RGN, FSE: B6H) said it has completed the acquisition of Landy Investments Ltd., through which the company gained the rights to two mineral properties in Nevada's Walker Lane Trend: the Hollow North-South project and the Douglas Canyon project. The release does not state the consideration paid for Landy Investments — no share issuance or cash amount is disclosed for the transaction. Hollow North-South, a copper-gold property, is located about 15 kilometres east of Yerington, Nevada, on 109 claims on land managed by the U.S. Bureau of Land Management. The release gives no further biographical detail. Separately, the company closed the second tranche of a non-brokered private placement, issuing 10,305,000 shares for gross proceeds of $1,030,500. The release does not disclose a price per share, warrant terms, or a closing date for the tranche, and does not name an agent or finder. Rush Gold said proceeds from the financing are intended to advance exploration on its existing and newly acquired mineral projects. The company reported cash on hand of $706,836 as of September 30, 2026, and said it had approximately 53.2 million shares outstanding. The company also said it has engaged CPS Capital Group and EuroSwiss Capital Partners on advisory, communications and marketing work intended to strengthen market awareness. Rush Gold said planned exploration activity across its Nevada projects includes geological mapping, geochemical sampling, geophysics and drill testing, without giving a timeline for any of the programs.

item.title: Argentum AI is negotiating $5 billion in debt to buy more AI chips
item.description: The Chicago-based neocloud, which already has $12 billion in contracted revenue, wants the financing to lease chips to customers without investment-grade credit.
item.content:encoded: Argentum AI, a Chicago-based cloud computing company backed by Super Micro, is in talks with a major private credit firm for a $5 billion financing deal, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing two people familiar with the matter. The debt would fund additional AI chips for a data centre Argentum is building in Poland with DL Invest Group. The financing is intended for chips leased to customers that do not carry investment-grade credit ratings, according to the sources. Argentum was founded in 2025 by chief executive Andrew Sobko and describes itself as an independent, institutional-grade AI cloud platform focused on deploying large-scale GPU infrastructure for enterprise AI. Argentum has more than $12 billion in contracted revenue, Reuters reported. The talks come a day after SpaceX secured $40 billion in debt financing for chips from an affiliate of Apollo Global Management, as financing has tightened for "neoclouds" — firms that rent out AI computing power. Elon Musk said "debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers," and predicted significant consolidation among the sector's more than 200 competitors. item.title: A proxy adviser is telling H&R REIT investors to reject a $3.4-billion buyout
item.description: ISS cited concerns about the sale process and an insider-linked side deal ahead of the November 13 unitholder vote on the GO Residential takeover.
item.content:encoded: Proxy adviser Institutional Shareholder Services is recommending that unitholders of H&R Real Estate Investment Trust vote against the trust's proposed $3.4-billion acquisition by GO Residential Real Estate Investment Trust, a deal announced in August. Under its terms, H&R unitholders would receive $4.28 in cash plus 0.5688 of a GO unit for every H&R unit they hold. The vote is scheduled for November 13. ISS's recommendation cited concerns over the sale process, conflicts of interest, the logic of the deal and whether disinterested unitholders are capturing fair value relative to insiders. The adviser pointed to a related transaction in which a company controlled by H&R chief executive Tom Hofstedter would acquire $1.98 billion of properties, at book value, for $1.56 billion — different consideration than other unitholders are receiving in the main transaction. Several institutional investors have already said publicly they intend to vote against the deal, including RBC Global Asset Management, Mill Pond Capital and Sandpiper Group. Rival proxy adviser Glass Lewis is expected to publish its own recommendation in the coming week. GO Residential's unit price has declined since the deal was announced, reducing the value of the consideration H&R unitholders would receive. H&R faces a $102-million termination fee if the transaction does not proceed. GO Residential Real Estate Investment Trust owns luxury apartments in New York. As part of the transaction, GO would issue 134.2 million of its own units to help fund the acquisition of $1.8 billion of residential properties. item.title: Red Canyon Resources closes $745,000 flow-through raise for BC critical minerals

item.content:encoded: Red Canyon Resources Ltd. (CSE: REDC) (OTCQB: REDRF) (Frankfurt: I91) has closed a non-brokered flow-through private placement for gross proceeds of $745,000. Red Canyon's release did not state whether this placement carried that kind of premium. Red Canyon is a Vancouver-based company exploring in British Columbia, trading on the CSE under REDC, on the OTCQB under REDRF, and in Frankfurt under I91. item.title: Nvidia is putting $3 billion into Meta's largest-ever fundraising round
item.description: The chipmaker's stake deepens a partnership on Meta's Muse AI assistant, built on Nvidia hardware, as Meta boosts its planned offering to $97.5 billion.
item.content:encoded: Nvidia is investing $3 billion in Meta Platforms' equity offering, which Meta increased to $97.5 billion. Reuters reported the enlarged raise is the largest fundraising in Meta's history. Meta is raising the money as it accelerates investment in AI infrastructure, Reuters reported. The deal deepens an existing partnership on Muse, Meta's personal AI assistant, internally known as Hatch, which runs on Nvidia infrastructure. Muse can access a user's email, calendar, payments, health, shopping and smart-home applications, with users able to revoke that access at any time, according to the reporting. The companies are also exploring joint work on Nvidia's OpenShell framework and a monitoring tool called Sentry, which is intended to track AI agent behaviour, Reuters reported. Chief executive Mark Zuckerberg has described Muse as central to delivering what he calls "personal superintelligence" to Meta's users; the system is modelled on the open-source AI agent OpenClaw, according to the reporting. item.title: Anthropic files for an IPO that could be the biggest ever
item.description: The AI company could raise up to $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, even as its chief executive warns of a risk to humanity from unchecked AI.
item.content:encoded: Anthropic has filed papers for an initial public offering that could be the largest in history, the Associated Press reported. The filing sets up a Wall Street debut as soon as next month, with the company potentially raising as much as $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion — topping the $86 billion raised by SpaceX's IPO in June, previously the record. Anthropic plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT. The company was founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI employees, including siblings Dario Amodei, its chief executive, and Daniela Amodei, its president. It reported revenue of more than $16 billion for the first half of 2026, fourteen times the prior year's figure, according to the AP. Anthropic also reported a net loss of $80.7 billion for the period, which includes a one-time accounting charge of $72.4 billion. The company has not yet reported a profit. Its seven founders are each expected to hold about 1.4% of the company, a stake that could be worth as much as $28 billion apiece at the top of the expected valuation range, the AP reported. The founders will retain 50.1% voting control through a special class of shares, and the company has established a Long-Term Benefit Trust of independent directors with the power to appoint board members, structured to keep financial interests from overriding public-safety considerations, according to the filing as reported by the AP. Dario Amodei has separately argued, in a post on his website, for slowing development of the most advanced AI models, warning that without an industry slowdown, AI could let loose "a swarm of agents" that could "take over the entire internet" within six to 12 months, the AP reported. The space theme on this publication's venture boards comprises two listed names; neither cleared the C$25,000 daily-volume floor this publication requires before naming a security today. No junior move is therefore reported alongside Anthropic's filing, and no names are given.

item.title: US and Canada edge toward a deal to ease steel and auto tariffs
item.description: Talks center on Section 232 duties of up to 50% on steel and 25% on autos, with Canadian sources saying a deal before the November 3 elections is possible but would likely be narrower in scope.
item.content:encoded: The United States and Canada are working on a deal to ease U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, Reuters reported, citing sources briefed on the talks. The negotiations aim to repair relations that soured after broader trade talks broke down in August, and focus on Section 232 duties — a US trade-law provision under which Washington has imposed tariffs of up to 50% on Canadian steel and 25% on Canadian autos. Trump has said he intends to raise the Canadian steel tariff to 50% from its current level starting January 1, 2027, absent a deal. He predicted at a political rally on Sunday that the trade dispute would be resolved "soon," without giving specifics, Reuters reported. Because Section 232 tariffs are administered by the US Commerce Department, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is at the center of the talks rather than the Office of the US Trade Representative, and Reuters reported he has been in regular contact with Canada's Dominic LeBlanc, the minister handling the file for Ottawa. A spokesperson for LeBlanc described the discussions as "constructive dialogue" on "a range of priorities." Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said there had been a "slight intensification" in talks, adding that "to the extent any progress has been made, it's because the US is coming closer to our position." One Canadian source briefed on the negotiations told Reuters that a deal was possible before the November 3 US midterm elections. A separate Canadian industry source told Reuters that any deal was likely to be "a narrowed deal" if it happens. Trump signed an order on Friday removing the 50% tariff on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, Reuters reported. This publication's tariffs theme produced no trading today, so there is no junior read-through to set alongside the talks: no venture name in the theme traded, leaving no group measure and no names to report, unlike the artificial-intelligence and space themes tracked elsewhere in this issue.

item.title: Ovintiv to acquire Logan Energy for C$1.26 billion
item.description: The all-cash deal adds about 266,000 net acres and 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day in the Montney's oil window, with closing expected early in 2027.
item.content:encoded: Ovintiv Inc. (NYSE:OVV, TSX:OVV) said it has agreed to acquire Logan Energy Corp. (TSXV:LGN) in an all-cash transaction. Logan shareholders will receive C$1.40 per share, for total consideration of approximately $890 million, or C$1.26 billion, including the assumption of Logan's net debt. The agreement was announced October 26, 2026, and the boards of both companies have unanimously approved it. The transaction brings Ovintiv roughly 266,000 net acres in the oil-rich window of the Montney formation, along with about 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day of current production, the release said. Ovintiv said the acreage carries approximately 420 net oil well locations drilled on a 10,000-foot equivalent lateral basis, including about 220 it classifies as premium return locations, at an average cost of $1.5 million per location, and roughly 200 as upside locations. The release said Logan's assets also include about 60,000 net acres with exposure to the Duvernay shale, two new oil batteries at Simonette with combined capacity of 24,000 barrels of oil a day, and interests in two natural gas processing facilities. These assets are included within the total consideration of approximately $890 million, or C$1.26 billion, that Ovintiv has agreed to pay, including the assumption of Logan's net debt. Ovintiv said the acquisition is expected to be accretive to its 2027 Non-GAAP Cash Flow per Share by approximately 5% and to its Non-GAAP Free Cash Flow per Share by approximately 3%. The company also said it expects annual cost synergies of about $60 million and capital savings of more than $2 million per well, and that its net debt is expected to be below $4 billion following the transaction's close. Ovintiv President and CEO Brendan McCracken said: "This bolt-on transaction delivers value for our shareholders by adding high margin oil and condensate production and infrastructure, utilizing our operational advantage to drive significant synergies, and adding to our already deep drilling inventory and future growth optionality." The release's own headline described the transaction as unlocking 'incremental profitability,' providing 'additional oil growth optionality' and adding to 'premium return drilling inventory.' Completion is expected early in the first quarter of 2027, subject to Logan shareholder approval, court approval, customary regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, the release said. RBC Capital Markets is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Ovintiv on the transaction, with Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP and Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP serving as Ovintiv's legal advisors. Ovintiv said its targeted shareholder returns are unchanged, with at least 60% of 2026 Non-GAAP Free Cash Flow expected to be returned to shareholders.

item.title: MetroCity Bankshares reports $24.3 million third-quarter net income
item.description: Diluted earnings per share rose to $0.84 for the quarter, with nine-month net income reaching $68.7 million, both ahead of the prior year.
item.content:encoded: MetroCity Bankshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: MCBS), the Atlanta-based holding company for Metro City Bank, reported net income of $24.3 million, or $0.84 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026 ended September 30, 2026, according to its earnings release dated October 23, 2026. The third-quarter result compares with net income of $22.1 million, or $0.76 per diluted share, in the second quarter of 2026, and with $17.3 million, or $0.67 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025 — increases of 9.8% and 40.7%, respectively, as stated in the release. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the company reported net income of $68.7 million, or $2.37 per diluted share, compared with $50.4 million, or $1.96 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 36.4%. For the third quarter, MetroCity reported return on average assets of 2.12%, return on average equity of 16.97% and a net interest margin of 4.07%, according to the release. At September 30, 2026, the company reported total assets of $4.60 billion, gross loans held for investment of $3.98 billion and total deposits of $3.56 billion. Noninterest-bearing deposits were $828.3 million, representing 23.3% of total deposits, and uninsured deposits represented 34.7% of total deposits. Dividends paid per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $0.87, compared with $0.71 for the same period in 2025. The release names Farid Tan as President and Interim Chief Financial Officer; no other executive is quoted. The release includes cautionary language stating that actual results could differ from any forward-looking statements due to factors including economic and market conditions, changes in interest rates, competitive pressures in the banking industry, and regulatory developments. It provides no additional guidance beyond the figures reported for the quarter and nine-month period.

item.title: Permian Basin Royalty Trust sets date for unitholder vote
item.description: Record date is October 13 and the special meeting is set for November 23, 2026, to vote on a proposed business combination and incentive plan.
item.content:encoded: Argent Trust Company, as trustee ('Trustee') of Permian Basin Royalty Trust (NYSE: PBT), announced on October 23, 2026 that it has set a record date of October 13, 2026 and a special meeting date of November 23, 2026 for unitholders to vote on proposals tied to a previously disclosed Business Combination. The special meeting was called at the request of SoftVest Advisors, LLC, together with other holders of trust units who, the release states, collectively own more than 15% of outstanding units. The first proposal asks unitholders to approve and adopt the terms of an amendment to the Trust Indenture to effect the Business Combination pursuant to a Combination Agreement. The second proposal asks unitholders to approve and adopt the terms of the PBT Land and Minerals, Inc. Omnibus Incentive Plan. The release does not describe what the plan covers beyond its name. The third proposal would authorize an adjournment of the special meeting, if necessary or appropriate, to permit the solicitation of additional proxies. The trustee states that it is not making any recommendation to unitholders as to how to vote on the proposals. It said additional details regarding the special meeting would be set forth in the trustee's notice, to be mailed to unitholders beginning October 23, 2026. For the substance of the Business Combination and the incentive plan, the release directs unitholders to the trust's Form S-4 and Form S-1 registration statements filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, rather than describing their terms itself.

item.title: Manufacturing sales edged up 0.1 percent in September
item.description: Statistics Canada's advance estimate points to gains led by petroleum and coal products and aerospace, with final figures due November 13.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada released an advance indicator on October 23, 2026 estimating that total manufacturing sales edged up 0.1% in September 2026. The agency said the largest increases were in the petroleum and coal product subsector and the aerospace product and parts industry group. The release gives no specific percentage change for either of those two groups, and no figures for any other subsector. Statistics Canada said the advance estimate is based on a weighted response rate of 71.3%, compared with an average final response rate of 92.4% over the preceding 12 months — a lower response rate that the agency says carries more risk of revision than a final estimate. The agency's official manufacturing sales figures for September 2026 are scheduled for release on November 13, 2026. The disclosure in this advance release is limited to the single aggregate figure, the two named industry groups, and the response-rate caveat; no further detail or commentary is given.

item.title: GOAT Industries to acquire casino contract revenues from Epoxy AI
item.description: The deal, paid in 11,377,600 GOAT shares at C$0.25 each, covers rights to six U.S. tribal casino and sportsbook contracts.
item.content:encoded: GOAT Industries Ltd. (CSE: GOAT) said its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Source Gaming Company, operating as BetSource, has entered into a definitive contract revenue assignment agreement dated October 20, 2026, with Epoxy AI, LLC. Under the agreement, Source Gaming will acquire customer contract revenues from Epoxy in exchange for 11,377,600 common shares of GOAT, issued at a price of C$0.25 per share. The rights being acquired cover revenues, receivables and other amounts payable under six customer contracts Epoxy holds with U.S. tribal casinos and other established casino and sports book operators. Rather than transferring the underlying contracts immediately, the agreement structures the deal as an assignment of the revenue stream from those contracts to Source Gaming. Epoxy is to formally assign the underlying customer contracts to Source Gaming within six months of closing, subject to the consent of the customers involved. Until that assignment takes place, the release said Epoxy will continue to perform its obligations under the contracts and will hold the resulting revenue in trust for Source Gaming. Completion of the transaction is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain conditions, including the release of applicable security interests, other necessary approvals, and acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. Either party may terminate the agreement if the transaction has not closed by November 30, 2026. Separately, the release said a US$100,000 non-interest-bearing promissory note dated January 2026 remains outstanding between the companies and will survive completion of the transaction. "This Agreement marks an important step forward in delivering on the strategy we outlined to shareholders," Hank Frecon, acting chief executive of Source Gaming Company, said in the release. The release described the transaction as advancing an acquisition strategy GOAT had previously outlined to shareholders in August 2026.

item.title: Howard Hughes Holdings set to join S&P SmallCap 600
item.description: The change follows CRH plc's acquisition of Arcosa Inc., which closed the same day, and takes effect before trading opens on October 28.
item.content:encoded: Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HHH) will replace Arcosa Inc. (NYSE: ACA) in the S&P SmallCap 600, S&P Dow Jones Indices said, effective before the opening of trading on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The index provider classified Howard Hughes under the Real Estate sector and had classified Arcosa under Industrials. The change was triggered by S&P 500 constituent CRH plc's (NYSE: CRH) acquisition of Arcosa, in a deal that closed the same day the index change was announced, October 23. S&P Dow Jones Indices describes itself as the largest global resource for index-based concepts, data and research, home to benchmarks including the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average, and said more assets are invested in products based on its indices than any other provider globally. It operates as a division of S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI). Beyond confirming that the CRH-Arcosa transaction had closed, the release disclosed no further terms of that acquisition, and gave no reason beyond the acquisition itself for Arcosa's removal from the index.

item.title: Hyperliquid Strategies boosts buyback authorization to $100 million
item.description: The board extended the program's expiration from December 2026 to October 31, 2027, and said about $72 million remains available for buybacks under the enlarged authorization.
item.content:encoded: Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. (Nasdaq: PURR) said its board of directors has authorized an increase to the company's stock repurchase program, raising the total authorization to $100 million from $30 million. The board also extended the program's termination date, pushing it out to October 31, 2027, from its original expiration of December 5, 2026. The company said approximately $72 million remains available for repurchases under the expanded authorization. A share repurchase, or buyback, program authorizes a company to buy back its own outstanding stock up to a set dollar amount, rather than committing it to purchase any fixed number of shares by a set date. The release said Hyperliquid Strategies may carry out repurchases through open market transactions, privately negotiated transactions, or other methods permitted under federal securities laws, with the timing, volume and price of any purchases left to management's discretion. The company describes itself as a digital asset treasury company built around HYPE, the native token of the Hyperliquid blockchain network, aiming to give U.S. and institutional investors capital-efficient exposure to the token through staking and yield strategies. The release said the increase "reflects the Board's confidence in the Company's long-term capital strategy and provides flexibility to buy back PURR shares as part of the Company's broader treasury management framework." The company said the timing, number and value of any shares repurchased will depend on the stock price, market conditions and legal requirements, and will remain at management's discretion. It said the board may extend, suspend or discontinue the program at any time without notice, and that there is no guarantee as to how many shares will ultimately be bought back. Beyond the dollar figures, the revised expiration date and the board's general statement of rationale, the release provides no additional detail on the buyback program.

item.title: Canadian retail sales rose 1.2% in August
item.description: Statistics Canada said sales reached $74.6 billion, with gains in all nine retail subsectors and a preliminary estimate pointing to a 0.7% rise in September.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada said retail sales in Canada rose 1.2% to $74.6 billion in August 2026, with increases recorded across all nine retail subsectors tracked in the survey. Motor vehicle and parts dealers posted the largest gain, also up 1.2%; gasoline stations rose 1.7%; and food and beverage retailers increased 1.1%, their first gain in three months, the agency said. Core retail sales, a measure that excludes gasoline stations and motor vehicle and parts dealers, rose 1.1% in August. In volume terms, which adjust the dollar figures for price changes, sales were also up 1.2%, indicating the increase reflected a rise in the quantity of goods sold rather than price alone. Provincial results varied. Ontario led with a 2.2% increase to $28.5 billion in retail sales, and British Columbia followed with a 2.1% increase to $10.0 billion. Sales declined in six provinces and territories — Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, New Brunswick, Alberta, Yukon and Nunavut — by between 0.1% and 0.6%, the agency said. E-commerce sales totalled $5.6 billion in August, up 1.1% from July and accounting for 7.6% of total retail trade for the month. Statistics Canada also published an advance estimate for September 2026, suggesting retail sales rose 0.7% for the month. The agency said the estimate is preliminary, based on a survey response rate of 58.5% compared with a historical average of 86.8%, and is subject to revision. The retail sales data are seasonally adjusted and reported in current dollars, the agency said.
